conventions.convention: Explicit tableaux have strictly lower-triangular A and row-sum abscissae c_i=sum_{j<i} a_ij; stages are queried in order, and domain or evaluation failure returns a status rather than a numerical value.
Local order p means a uniform exact-start method-minus-exact defect O(h^(p+1)); order assertions inherit the stated smoothness and compact-tube hypotheses.
RKC1 permits s≥1; both RKC2 algorithms require s≥2. Nonlinear RKC2 uses b_0=b_1=b_2=1/4, c_0=0, c_1=b_1 w_1, and c_j=b_j w_1 j² for j≥2.
The RKC1 real stability set is exactly [-2s²,0]; the displayed RKC2 interval is certified rather than claimed maximal. Euclidean nonexpansion requires a self-adjoint nonpositive operator.
Stage perturbations are additive vectors inserted after recurrence updates, with the initial state unperturbed; their assumed norm bound is not a floating-point error estimate.

Nonlinear RKC2 accuracy and one-step stability constants may depend on fixed s and the tube; global error additionally requires the numerical trajectory and stages to remain admitted in the common tube.
SSP preservation assumes forward-Euler preservation at the actual stage start times t, t+h, and t+h/2; the functional estimates bound every stage and output by the initial functional value.

load_bearing.statement: An explicit s-stage tableau has a_ij=0 whenever j≥i and c_i=sum_{j<i} a_ij. Its ordered stages are Y_i=y+h sum_{j<i} a_ij K_j, K_i=f(t+c_i h,Y_i), with candidate output y+h sum_i b_i K_i and explicit domain/evaluation failure statuses.

For every natural n, |T_n(x)|≤1 and |U_n(x)|≤n+1 on [-1,1], with T_n(±1) and U_n(±1) as stated. For n≥1, |T_n(x)|>1 when |x|>1; T_n and U_n have degree n and leading coefficients 2^(n-1) and 2^n. T_n'(1)=n² and T_n''(1)=n²(n²-1)/3.

For an explicit row-sum tableau and a C^4 autonomous field on an open convex domain, with exact solution and exact-start stages in a common compact convex set and derivatives through order four bounded there, the displayed coefficient equations through each p≤4 suffice for uniform local order at least p.

RKC1 has R_1,s(z)=T_s(1+z/s²) and exact real stability set [-2s²,0]. Both linear RKC2 and nonlinear RKC2 specialized to the scalar linear equation have R_2,s(z)=a_s+b_s T_s(1+w_1 z), normalized through the second derivative at zero and stable on [-2(s²-1)/3,0]. The corresponding spectral restrictions imply Euclidean nonexpansion for self-adjoint nonpositive matrices.

Under the order-condition supplier's smoothness and compact-tube hypotheses, Euler, explicit midpoint, and classical RK4 have uniform local orders at least one, two, and four. Their scalar stability polynomials are the exponential truncations through degrees one, two, and four; Euler and midpoint have negative-real stability interval exactly [-2,0].

For the stated self-adjoint nonpositive operator and certified RKC spectral interval, additive recurrence perturbations of norm at most ε give final stage error at most s(s+1)ε/2. Linear RKC2 multiplies that error by b_s; a separate output perturbation adds its norm.
